The Algemeen Dagblad newspaper agreed. ""What is going to happen on the 30th of April next year? And will we continue to see the members of the royal family cycling through the canals of Amsterdam or hunting for bargains in the Bijenkorf in The Hague?" Although Queen Beatrix's birthday is January 31, she officially celebrates her birthday April 30, according to the Dutch government. Queen's Day is known for its free market all over the country, where anybody is allowed to sell things in the streets. Other activities include children's games and musical performances. # Suspect in Attack on Dutch Royal Family Dies of Injuries

(CNN) -- The man suspected of attempting to attack the Dutch royal family by driving his car toward their bus has died, Dutch police announced Friday.

The suspect, whose identity has not been disclosed, sustained serious injuries in Thursday's crash in the town of Apeldoorn, located approximately 45 miles east of Amsterdam. He succumbed to his injuries early Friday morning, according to police. He had been charged with attempting to attack the royal family, authorities confirmed.

A search of the man's residence yielded no weapons, explosives, "or any other clues that could lead to the involvement of other people," police reported.

The incident, which occurred during the country's annual Queen's Day celebrations, claimed the lives of five bystanders in addition to the driver, and left 12 others injured. Crowds had gathered along the streets to watch Queen Beatrix and her family pass by in an open-top bus, a cherished tradition of this Dutch national holiday.

As the royal bus proceeded along its route, a black hatchback suddenly accelerated past it. While spectators remained safely behind barriers, security personnel and members of the press—including numerous cameramen—were stationed in the road itself as the vehicle sped through. The car ultimately collided with a low metal railing surrounding a roadside column. Notably, the vehicle appeared significantly damaged even prior to the crash, though the cause of this damage remains unclear. Police spokeswoman Esther Naber confirmed that the driver was alone in the vehicle at the time of the incident.

Members of the royal family witnessed the crash and reacted with visible shock, gasping before quickly taking their seats as the bus continued on its route.

## National Reaction

The attack sparked widespread outrage throughout the Netherlands, with Friday's newspapers expressing profound disbelief while suggesting that the monarchy's approach to public engagement may need to change.

"Queen's Day will never be the same," declared the newspaper *Trouw*. "The Netherlands has always taken pride in its unpretentious royal family. This includes a Queen who not only rides a bicycle but also mingles with the public without conspicuous security measures. Is this still feasible now that the royal family has been the target of an attack?"

The newspaper *Algemeen Dagblad* echoed these sentiments, posing pointed questions: "What will happen on April 30th next year? Will we continue to see members of the royal family cycling along Amsterdam's canals or hunting for bargains at the Bijenkorf in The Hague?"

## About Queen's Day

Queen's Day stands as a national holiday celebrated in the Netherlands, the Netherlands Antilles, and Aruba. Established in 1885, the tradition honors the reigning queen's birthday. Although Queen Beatrix was actually born on January 31, she officially observes her birthday on April 30, in accordance with Dutch governmental custom.

The holiday is renowned for its nationwide free markets, where anyone is permitted to sell goods in the streets, alongside children's games and musical performances. Throughout the celebration, the color orange dominates the festivities—a tribute to the royal House of Orange-Nassau.

*Emmy Dexel contributed to this report.*

# Suspect in Dutch Royal Attack Dies From Injuries

(CNN) -- Dutch authorities announced Friday that the individual believed to have targeted the Netherlands' royal family by driving his vehicle toward their bus has passed away from his injuries.

According to police, the unidentified man sustained critical injuries during Thursday's incident in Apeldoorn, a town located roughly 45 miles from Amsterdam. His death occurred in the early hours of Friday. Officials had already brought charges against him for the attempted assault on the royal family.

**Witnesses invited to share footage and photos**

Authorities conducted a search of the suspect's residence but turned up nothing—no weapons, no explosive materials, and nothing suggesting other individuals were involved in planning the attack.

The tragic incident, which unfolded during the Netherlands' beloved Queen's Day festivities, claimed six lives total (including the driver) and left a dozen people injured.

## How the Incident Unfolded

Spectators had gathered along the parade route to catch a glimpse of Queen Beatrix and her family traveling in an open-top vehicle as part of the traditional holiday celebration.

While the royal bus proceeded along its path, a dark-colored hatchback suddenly sped past. Although the general public remained behind protective barriers away from the roadway, numerous security personnel and members of the press—including camera operators—were positioned within the street itself when the vehicle sped through.

The car ultimately collided with a metal barrier surrounding a roadside pillar. Notably, the vehicle showed significant damage that predated the crash, though authorities couldn't immediately explain this. Police spokesperson Esther Naber confirmed the driver was alone in the vehicle.

Royal family members witnessed the collision, reacting with visible shock before taking their seats as the bus continued on its route.

## National Reaction

The event sparked widespread outrage throughout the country, with Friday's newspapers expressing collective shock while questioning whether the monarchy's approach to public engagement would need reconsideration.

"Queens Day will never be the same," declared the Trouw newspaper. The publication noted the Dutch tradition of pride in their unpretentious royal family—one where the Queen bikes casually and mingles freely with citizens, often without heavy security. The paper questioned whether this openness could continue following an attack targeting the royals.

The Algemeen Dagblad newspaper echoed similar concerns, asking what changes might come to next year's celebration and whether royal family members would still be seen cycling along Amsterdam's canals or browsing for deals at The Hague's Bijenkorf department store.

## Background on Queen's Day

This national holiday, observed in the Netherlands, the Netherlands Antilles, and Aruba, dates back to 1885 and honors the monarch's birthday. Despite Queen Beatrix actually being born January 31, the Dutch government designates April 30 as the official celebration date.

The holiday is particularly famous for its nationwide free markets, where citizens can sell goods on the streets without restriction. Festivities also typically include games for children and live musical entertainment. Orange—the signature color of the House of Orange-Nassau, the royal family's lineage—dominates celebrations throughout the country on this day.

*Emmy Dexel contributed to this report.*
